traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Elatinaceae: leaves usually opposite, rarely whorled; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate or serrate; veins pinnate; blades linear, lanceolate, oblanceolate, oblong, ovate or obovate; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 2 to 5 (-6); stamens 2 to 10 (-12); carpels 2 to 5 (-6). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
